purpose: Bind constitutional authority, HITL decision-to-effect evidence, continuous claim maintenance and protocol projections without making any one engine mandatory.

runtime_executor: OpenShell or another separately authorized executor

separation_rules: payment or signature never grants execution authority
a claim that is not CURRENT is not authority to act
an APPROVE is bound to a current external authority record, not to a chat, a ticket or a person present at the time
an unknown revocation state fails closed
an unknown watch state is not CURRENT

interfaces.MCP: read/write capability boundary subject to separate authority
interfaces.A2A: delegation/evidence boundary subject to separate authority

limits: This manifest is a CSOAI candidate contract, not an Alliance standard.
OpenShell, OpenBMC, LFX and vendor profiles are optional adapters, not authorities.
Signatures, transparency receipts and timestamps establish scoped provenance/time properties only.

Version 0.3 supersedes 0.2 by pointing the HITL profile at hitl-authority-effect-v0.2. The 0.2 bytes and the v0.1 schema bytes are preserved unchanged; superseding is a new record, never an edit of history.

The v0.2 HITL schema binds a claim that is not CURRENT to no authorization, and binds an APPROVE to a current external authority record. It does not resolve that external record, authenticate the principal, or prove that the reviewed scope actually executed.
